description: Polyphonic trigger generator whose pulse timing runs anywhere from perfectly regular to the random statistics of radioactive decay

params.text: Sets the mean pulse rate from -7 to +7, each unit doubling it, with 0 giving 2Hz, +7 giving 256Hz and -7 giving about one pulse a minute
Attenuates and inverts the speed CV; fully clockwise the CV input tracks a volt per octave
Sets how irregular the timing is: at 0 the pulses fall at exactly fixed intervals, at 1 they follow Poisson statistics with no regularity, and values between interpolate
Attenuates and inverts the chaos CV
Restarts every polyphonic pulse engine in sync, which is useful for bringing the channels to a common starting point when the timing is nearly regular
Switches the output between triggers and gates
Holds the output at 0V and keeps every engine reset; the next trigger at SYNC releases it and turns this button off

inputs.text: Varies the mean pulse rate; with its attenuverter fully clockwise it tracks a volt per octave
Varies how irregular the pulse timing is
A trigger here restarts the pulse engines in sync; a polyphonic cable syncs each channel on its own, and its last channel is repeated across any remaining ones

outputs.text: In trigger mode each pulse takes that channel to 10V for one millisecond and then to 0V for another, so pulses can occur at up to 500Hz; in gate mode each pulse toggles the channel between 0V and 10V

menu: Output channels — sets how many independent pulse generators run, 1 to 16, and the number appears on the panel display
Send trigger on every reset — fires a pulse the moment a sync arrives, in place of the random delay that otherwise follows a reset
Sync polyphonic channels — restarts every pulse engine together, the same action as the sync button on the panel
Output pulse mode — chooses Triggers or Gates, doing by menu what the pulse mode button does
Configure for V/OCT — on the SPEED attenuverter's own menu, not the panel menu: sets that attenuverter so the speed CV tracks a volt per octave
Low sensitivity — on an attenuverter knob's own menu, not the panel menu: divides that knob's effect by 10 and marks the knob with an orange dot
Unipolar mode — on an attenuverter knob's own menu, not the panel menu: adds 5V to the CV on that control and clamps the result at zero

inputs.1:
continuous · polyphonic

a negative voltage subtracts from the knob; the knob and this input are summed and the total held to ±5V.
